subject: Safekeep BYO-K deployment — operator handoff, sealed-key escrow and warden-proxy egress
messages:
From: Rajesh Kapoor <rajesh.kapoor@safekeep.io>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com; dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Safekeep Security <security@safekeep.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial: Safekeep BYO-K deployment — questions on operator handoff and egress constraints

Hi Vanessa / Dylan,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing the on-prem BYO-K rollout for our Goodwatch tenant and need to lock down a handful of operational constraints before the cutover:

- We will be using our HSM cluster (Safekeep HSM-Prod) for root signing; we need to confirm the operator handoff model you support for sealed-key escrow. Specifically: do you require an intermediate key-wrapping proxy (we've heard you refer to a "warden-proxy") or can Redwood operate with an ephemeral wrapping token issued to our operator identity?
- Attestation evidence: what exact files/assertions do you provide post-ceremony? We expect an HSM attestation blob, signed key manifest, and rotation schedule.
- Network egress: our security team requires that any egress to Redwood control plane occurs only from a fixed IP range and is TLS-mutual. We also have strict DNS/pinning requirements. Can you confirm allowed ports, IP ranges, and whether mutual TLS for the operator agent is supported?
- Rotation windows and operator access: we need a minimal downtime rotation path and a fail-closed emergency revoke method.

I've attached our current network diagram (safekeep_current_network_v1.pdf). Can you propose a checklist or runbook we can validate against?

Proposed attendees for the design review: myself (Rajesh), Safekeep Sec lead (Elena), Vanessa (Redwood RM), Marcus (Redwood crypto infra), and one of our network engineers.

Thanks,
Rajesh Kapoor
Head of Infrastructure
Safekeep
[Attachment: safekeep_current_network_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Safekeep BYO-K deployment — questions on operator handoff and egress constraints

Rajesh — thanks for the clear list and the diagram. Attaching a concise Redwood checklist that maps to each ask so we can review line-by-line in the design review.

Short answers up front:
- Warden-proxy vs ephemeral token: we support both patterns. For customers with strict airgap/attestation requirements we recommend a warden-proxy (an optional lightweight service you run in your VPC) that performs key wrapping and strictly controls egress to our control plane. For customers who prefer operator-managed ephemeral tokens we can provide a one-time ephemeral-wrap protocol (short-lived) with recorded attestations.
- Attestation artifacts: we provide (1) HSM attestation blob (vendor-signed), (2) signed key manifest with key-hash and UUID, (3) ceremony transcript (who/when), and (4) rotation schedule records exported as CSV/JSON.
- Mutual TLS + IP allowlist: supported. Our operator agent supports mTLS to our control plane endpoints; you can pin using SAN or exact cert CN. We'll provide the IP ranges used by Redwood control plane and support source IP allowlisting from your firewall.
- Rotation windows: we recommend a rolling wrap/unwrap with a 5–15 minute per-key window (depends on QPS). For emergency revokes we support an immediate key-blacklist and crossing-rollover to a standby key stored in your HSM.

Action items for the review:
1) Marcus to propose the warden-proxy architecture and required ports.
2) Redwood to produce an attestation example and sample manifest (Marcus).
3) Safekeep to confirm desired operator model (warden-proxy vs ephemeral token) and dates for a dry-run.

Attaching: redwood_byo_handshake_checklist.pdf (checklist + example runbook).

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: redwood_byo_handshake_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: Safekeep BYO-K deployment — questions on operator handoff and egress constraints

On Tue, Jun 22, 2026 at 10:03 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Rajesh — thanks for the clear list and the diagram. Attaching a concise Redwood checklist that maps to each ask so we can review line-by-line in the design review.

Thanks — adding technical detail so the team has a concrete proposal before the call.

High-level warden-proxy design (draft):
- Purpose: keep all long-term key material inside customer's HSM; warden-proxy performs ephemeral wrapping/unwrapping and enforces egress policy.
- Deployment: single-node service (HA optional) deployed in Safekeep VPC in the same subnet as the HSM gateway. Communicates to HSM over the local network (KMIP/TLS) and to Redwood control plane over mTLS.
- Auth model: mutual TLS with client certs bound to the warden-proxy identity. We rotate the proxy cert via ACME/automatic issuance or via your KMS-based CA; rotation window is 30 days by default (configurable).
- Network: outbound to Redwood control plane uses TLS 1.3, ports 443 + 44301 for mutual endpoints. We will provide the precise IP CIDR list in the design doc; if you prefer FQDN pinning we support that too.
- Key wrapping flow:
  1) Operator triggers wrap request to warden-proxy.
  2) Proxy requests an ephemeral wrapping key from customer's HSM (KMIP Generate/Wrap).
  3) Proxy wraps the key and ships wrapped blob to Redwood (control plane).
  4) Redwood stores wrapped blob and returns a key manifest and certificate of possession.
  5) For rotations, proxy supports a zero-downtime staggered wrap (dual-write to new and old wrapper IDs) with reconcile logic.

Attestation evidence we will provide (example payloads):
- HSM vendor attestation (binary blob)
- Signed key manifest (json, includes key UUID, SHA-256 of public key, wrapping algorithm, timestamp)
- Ceremony transcript (human-readable log, signed by proxied operator identity)

Operational constraints / preflight checklist (summary):
- Allowlist Redwood outgoing CIDRs: (will publish; temporary preflight list included in doc)
- Ports: 443 (mTLS), 22 (admin bastion optional), 5222 (proxy heartbeats)
- Logging: proxy must forward audit logs to your Splunk/Graylog endpoint; Redwood will ingest manifest-level telemetry only (no raw key material).
- Fail-closed: proxy supports explicit emergency revoke API that returns 403 for subsequent wrap requests and pushes a blacklist to Redwood.

I've dropped a rough design into the shared folder and attached a plain-text sequence diagram (warden-proxy-design-draft.md) for quick review.

Let me know if you want a simplified ephemeral-token path instead; that path reduces infra in your VPC but requires you to accept a one-time proof of possession exchange.

— Marcus Lin
Principal Crypto Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: warden-proxy-design-draft.md (text)]
